answer: Admission can be throttled by churn instead of by price. Each epoch it opens only as many new slots as seats lost to slashing or retirement, drawn by beacon from a public queue; no purchase moves you up. A farm wanting a thousand seats must wait for a thousand honest exits, and its own burned seats return slots to the queue, so attacking replenishes what throttles it. The cost is calendar time, which no farm parallelizes: each clone is a stone set into a basalt queue, not a ripple of free accounts. Honest newcomers wait it once, a brief haven, while a hundred clones queue behind them.
